Hydropower Application: Monitor hydropower turbine operating conditions to estimate and track machine efficiency under varying load, discharge, and environmental conditions.
RAI Technology Detail: Supervised machine-learning–based performance estimation and efficiency modeling
Supporter role: Y (interpretation and maintenance judgment improve reliability)
Requirement:
• Plant sensors measuring load, discharge, head, current, and bearing oil/metal temperatures
• Plant data acquisition and monitoring system (historical operational data)
• Computing environment for statistical modeling and periodic model inference
Performance:
• ANN model achieved R² = 0.99966, MAPE = 0.0239%, and RMSPE = 0.1785%, outperforming curve fitting and multilinear regression
• High agreement between predicted and calculated efficiency across training, validation, and testing datasets
• Results indicate suitability for real-time or near-real-time efficiency monitoring
Limitations:
• Model validated on one Kaplan-turbine hydropower plant only
• Requires high-quality historical plant data for training
• Transferability to other turbine types or sites not demonstrated
Citation: (Kumar et al. 2024)

Task: Operate high voltage switches or related devices in hydropower stations.
Application_Grouping: Equipment Fault Diagnosis and Predictive Maintenance
Hydropower Application: Detect operating conditions consistent with equipment faults in hydropower plants to support timely maintenance response.
RAI Technology Detail: Unsupervised machine-learning–based fault and anomaly detection combined with multivariate statistical monitoring
Requirement:
• Plant-mounted sensors measuring vibration, bearing metal temperature, bearing oil temperature, and active power
• Data acquisition and monitoring systems (e.g., SCADA or equivalent)
• Computing environment for continuous or periodic data analytics and model inference
Performance:
• Successfully identified fault periods in two real hydropower plants using operational data
• Fault indicators exceeded control limits during known fault events, aligning with manually recorded maintenance logs
• In some cases, abnormal conditions were detected hours before manual fault recognition
Limitations:
• Validation limited to two plants and a relatively short observation period
• Requires representative nominal (fault-free) data for training
• Does not identify physical root causes or specific faulty components
• Final fault confirmation and maintenance decisions remain human-driven
Citation: Hajimohammadali, F.; Fontana, N.; Tucci, M.; Crisostomi, E.

• Plant-mounted sensors measuring vibration, bearing metal temperature, bearing oil temperature, and active power
• Data acquisition and monitoring systems (e.g., SCADA or equivalent)
• Computing environment for continuous or periodic data analytics and model inference

• Successfully identified fault periods in two real hydropower plants using operational data
• Fault indicators exceeded control limits during known fault events, aligning with manually recorded maintenance logs

• Validation limited to two plants and a relatively short observation period
• Requires representative nominal (fault-free) data for training
• Does not identify physical root causes or specific faulty components
• Final fault confirmation and maintenance decisions remain human-driven
